question: Lichtenberg figures (branching, fern-like skin markings) are pathognomonic of lightning injury and persist on the skin for weeks after death, making them reliable for delayed forensic examination.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect — partially. Lichtenberg figures ARE pathognomonic of lightning (correct) but they FADE rapidly (within hours to days). Always photograph them immediately at the scene or first PM examination. They will not be present at a delayed examination.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is PARTIALLY FALSE. While Lichtenberg figures ARE pathognomonic of lightning injury (that part is true), they FADE within hours to a few days. This makes early documentation (photography at the scene or initial PM examination) essential. They are NOT reliable at delayed forensic examination.
